decisions.executionNote: Begin left tube approach by lifting and pitching the left wrist, maintaining elbow-up continuity; right arm stays parked.
Advance above the left tube, gradually matching its diagonal tabletop axis with the open gripper.
Align downward over the left tube and descend to a pregrasp height; use the next wrist view to refine centering.
Refine left grasp toward the cap-side body and lower slowly; tube axis and camera offset remain slightly uncertain.
Slide the open left grasp along the tube body toward its cap; wrist view indicates the previous alignment was too near the tapered end.
Close the left gripper around the centered tube body, then hold before lifting to check retention visually.
Lift the closed left grasp clear of the tabletop and retreat slightly before uprighting the tube.
Tube appears retained. Begin a smooth upright rotation while carrying it toward the rack's left side.
Continue bringing the retained tube upright over the left rack region, keeping the gripper closed.
Finish uprighting the first tube and align above a left rack slot before descending.
Lower the upright first tube toward the left slot, stopping above full insertion for a wrist-camera alignment check.
Guide the first tube down into the left opening with a small lateral correction, retaining the grasp until seated.
Open the first grasp and withdraw slightly to inspect whether the tube is supported upright in the slot; contact may already have seated its tip.
Clear the first tube with the open left hand and start an elbow-up approach to the nearer central-right tube. Check the released tube's stability.
The first tube has tipped out and will need recovery. Clear the left arm while aligning the right wrist above the central-right tabletop tube.
Finish aligning the right open gripper to the central-right tube and lower to a pregrasp height, while retracting the left arm.
Lower the right gripper around the tube body with a small capward adjustment; complete the left arm's retreat near origin.
Refine the right gripper's axial alignment and close around the tube body, holding still before the lift.
Lift the right tube clear of the table while keeping the grasp closed; inspect retention before uprighting.
Begin uprighting the retained right tube while moving toward the rack's right-side openings.
Continue the right tube's upright rotation and approach, remaining above the rack and keeping the grasp closed.
Finish making the right tube vertical above the right rack slot; check the tip-to-opening alignment before insertion.
Align the upright right tube toward a large front-right opening and lower only to the slot approach height for another visual check.
Lower the vertical right tube in small increments; monitor whether it enters the opening or shifts within the fingers on contact.
Continue the slow vertical insertion of the right tube, checking for contact-induced slipping before release.
Tube appears to have contacted a rim rather than descended. Apply a millimeter-scale right/front correction before a short insertion test; do not release yet.
The tube is not clearly seated. Lift away from the rim and reposition farther back over the large opening rather than releasing an unstable tube.
Test a slow insertion at the corrected, farther-back alignment while retaining the tube.
Lift clear of the obstructed rim and shift toward the adjacent large opening, keeping the right tube upright and retained.
Make a small centering correction over the adjacent large slot, then lower the retained tube while watching for continued downward motion.
Adjust the right tube a few millimeters toward the opening center and test another short vertical insertion while retaining it.
The tube has descended at the corrected opening. Release gradually without withdrawing so it can settle into the slot, then check upright support.
Withdraw the open right hand to verify that the released tube remains upright; lift the left wrist to recover the fallen tube.
The right tube remains supported in the rack. Retract that hand and approach the fallen tube with the left hand, gradually matching its reversed axis.
Continue the left recovery approach above the fallen tube with gradual rotation; move the right hand safely toward home.
Position the downward left hand over the fallen tube and continue rotating its open grasp toward the tube axis; finish retracting the right arm.
Rotate the left grasp along the fallen tube while lowering to pregrasp height. Keep the wrist rotation continuous and the right hand near home.
Center the left fingers around the recovered tube and lower gently, using only a small further wrist turn to preserve rotation margin.
Close on the recovered tube body, then make a small vertical retention-check lift without further wrist winding.
Lift the recovered left tube clear of the rack and tabletop before unwinding and uprighting the retained grasp.
Unwind the left wrist along a continuous upright-turn path while holding the recovered tube clear of the rack.
Continue the gradual left-wrist unwinding and upright rotation, retaining clearance above the rack and the closed grasp.
Continue uprighting the recovered tube while approaching the left rack region, maintaining the closed grasp and elbow-up configuration.
Finish the recovered tube's upright turn above the left side of the rack, then inspect its actual axis and slot alignment.
The recovered tube appears tilted toward the wrist. Correct its actual axis while compensating the wrist position to keep the grasp center nearly fixed above the rack.
Move the recovered tube above a large left-front opening rather than the edge, descending only to an approach height for visual centering.
Lower the recovered tube toward the large left-front slot with a slight centering adjustment, retaining the grasp for another visual check.
Center the recovered tube tip over the visible large opening, then test a short downward insertion without releasing.
The recovered tube tip appears centered over the large slot. Open gradually in place to let it settle, then inspect support before withdrawing.
The recovered tube is leaning rather than settling. Reclose to arrest the tilt and lift slightly before another alignment attempt.
